scope.summary: Close the loose ends MT-142 handed off honestly rather than fixed: seven test-side defects and one product defect among the eight carried pre-existing failures; the three stated limits that are testable; the research-basis citation defect; the dirty_meaning typo; and the early-lock-release residual, by making the lock-only invariants in stores MT-142 did not own safe under the now-global caller-side statement bound. Explicitly NOT in scope: title-anchor reclamation (stays routed with its reason), the full migration of the other product-data locks onto the MT-142 primitives (D-142-1 follow-on), and any investigation of RSS growth (a recorded finding).

items.title: schema.rs assertion drift
items.detail: schema.rs:3353 asserts the pre-4ed7b60a wording of the atelier_source_evidence_record ASSERT; schema.surql:1955 now reads `$value = type::record('atelier_source_evidence_record', [$this.matrix_id, record::id($value)[1]])`. Update the assertion to the current statement. schema.rs:3908 fixture writes task_board_status 'ready'; the product contract is SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (schema.surql:609, locus/types.rs:1009). Write 'READY'.

items.title: loom_edges projector record identity
items.detail: knowledge.rs:1484 and wiki_store.rs:1151 create backlink edges with CREATE loom_edges CONTENT { edge_id ... } and a RANDOM record id, while loom_store.rs:1218 creates its own edges deterministically and delete_loom_edge (loom_store.rs:1263-1277) resolves by record id. Fix option (a) from the triage: create the projected edge at the deterministic record id type::record('loom_edges', $row.relationship_id) at both sites, so pre-fix rows self-migrate on the next backlink rebuild. Do NOT add the schema alias ASSERT (option c) in this MT: it would bite existing random-id rows on their next write. State the persisted random-id row count if you can measure it cheaply, otherwise UNVERIFIED.

items.title: knowledge_claims_tests inspector decoding and PostgreSQL wording
items.detail: inspected_row_field (tests/knowledge_claims_tests.rs:88-116) must unwrap the inspector's externally tagged values the way scalar() does in tests/wp_kernel_012_native_editor_routes_tests.rs (single-entry tag object; bare None/Null mean absent; RecordId collapses to its key). Two assertions (:979 and :553) still demand the PostgreSQL text 'foreign key'; the product now surfaces the real Surreal record::exists ASSERT message via meaningful_check - assert on the Surreal wording or on the typed error class, never on PostgreSQL text.

items.title: early-lock-release residual (RESIDUAL-MT142-EARLY-LOCK-RELEASE-ON-STATEMENT-TIMEOUT)
items.detail: The caller-side statement bound in SurrealStorage::with_data_operation now wraps every store, so a 300 s timeout drops the LOOM_/CANVAS_/OVERLAY_/MARKDOWN_IMPORT_/WIKI_COMPILE_/BLOCK_VIEW_/BRIDGE_/DEPENDENCY_ mutex guard while the abandoned statement may still be live. Audit every invariant those mutexes protect (MT-142 recon lock_inventory.json other_global_locks lists them with sites; the recon flagged the Loom journal get-or-create and the Canvas/Wiki identity-choice paths as lock-only candidates). For each invariant that is ALSO enforced database-side (UNIQUE index, THROW guard, CAS) record that and move on. For each invariant that is LOCK-ONLY, add the database-side guard (a UNIQUE index or an in-transaction THROW) so early release is safe, and prove it with a test that races the path with the lock registry disabled. Fallback, only where a guard is not cheap: exclude that specific store from the caller-side bound with a written reason in a doc comment, so it returns to its pre-MT-142 behaviour rather than gaining a new window. Do NOT migrate those stores onto guarded_mutation/keyed locks in this MT (D-142-1 follow-on).

items.title: exercise no_retry_window against a live saturation event
items.detail: MT-142 left HSK-STORAGE-NO-RETRY-WINDOW wired but unexercised (count 0 on every clean run). Add a deterministic test that forces it: open a store, set a small with_statement_timeout so the shared budget is tiny, make the first attempt slow enough to consume it (a SurrealQL SLEEP inside the retried statement, or a held keyed lock released only after the budget), and assert the typed HSK-STORAGE-NO-RETRY-WINDOW outcome with attempts == 1, distinct from HSK-STORAGE-RETRY-EXHAUSTED. Then feed the same outcome through the swarm classifier and assert no_retry_window.count == 1 and that it never lands in expected_stale_or_conflict.

items.title: cover the zero-remaining-budget branch
items.detail: with_data_operation refuses to dispatch when the OPERATION_DEADLINE task-local has already passed and returns SurrealStorageError::StatementBudgetExhausted { budget_ms }. Cover it with a unit test that sets an already-expired deadline and asserts the typed error and that no statement was issued (a resume-path store or the kv-mem dev engine is fine; a fresh cold apply is not required).

items.title: prove the two serialization mechanisms redundant
items.detail: Run the three swarm targets once WITHOUT RUST_TEST_THREADS set, relying only on the in-code SWARM_SERIAL mutex, and record the result lines. If they pass, the env var is proven an optimisation and the runbook says so; if they fail, say why and keep the env var as a requirement.
closes: stated limit: serialization mechanisms not proven redundant

items.title: research-basis citation and dirty_meaning typo
items.detail: In ../Handshake_Artifacts/WP-KERNEL-012-Native-Editors-Obsidian-VSCode-Parity-v1/MT-142/kb01/research/research_basis.json the RSS-growth entry cites upstream #7411; #7411 is the TransactionFinished defect and the RSS pointer is #7424 (related #7383) - correct it and note the correction. In tests/surreal_swarm_load_tests.rs:1790 the dirty_meaning literal drops a word ('does not correspond to  and'); name the sibling field: 'does not correspond to head, and this artifact ...'.

acceptance_criteria: AC-151-1: all eight carried tests are green on the embedded store, with no assertion weakened - a PostgreSQL wording assertion is replaced by the Surreal wording or the typed error class, never deleted.

AC-151-2: projected loom_edges rows are created at the deterministic record id used by loom_store, and delete_loom_edge removes a projector-created edge; existing random-id rows are not migrated by schema and the count of such rows is stated or marked UNVERIFIED.

AC-151-3: every invariant protected by a remaining process-global storage mutex is either recorded as database-guarded with the guard named, or gains a database-side guard proven by a lock-registry-disabled race test, or the store is excluded from the caller-side bound with a written reason; no lock-only invariant remains exposed to early release.
AC-151-4: HSK-STORAGE-NO-RETRY-WINDOW and StatementBudgetExhausted each have a deterministic test that produces them, and the swarm classifier counts the former distinctly.
AC-151-5: the swarm targets have been run once without RUST_TEST_THREADS and the outcome is recorded either way.
AC-151-6: no PostgreSQL or SQLite token is introduced (AC-142-9 scan repeated); crate warnings do not increase; every changed target has a verbatim green result line at the final commit.

cargo test --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml --test knowledge_claims_tests --features surreal-test-support,test-utils -j 4 --no-fail-fast -- --nocapture   # expect 7 passed

cargo test --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml --test surreal_swarm_semantics_tests --features surreal-test-support,test-utils -j 4 --no-fail-fast -- --nocapture   # plus load and lifecycle, once with RUST_TEST_THREADS unset
